key_risks.description: Industry-wide memory shortage and rising memory prices could raise AMD's production costs and compress gross margin, and may push up data center buildout costs, which could delay or reduce customer demand.

Customers may lack or be unable to secure capital to fund AI infrastructure and may request alternative financing or deferred-payment arrangements from vendors and suppliers. AMD also has data center lease guarantees with maximum potential future payments of $4.1 billion.

Unconditional commitments of approximately $30.3 billion, of which $17.4 billion falls in the remainder of fiscal 2026. Also $4.5 billion of leases not yet commenced and long-term data center leases with $9.5 billion of aggregate future payments commencing in 2027 and 2028. These are fixed claims on cash if AI demand slows.
Customer concentration: a small number of customers is expected to account for a substantial part of revenue, and the loss of a significant customer may have a material adverse effect.

Helios rack-scale platform, expected to start shipping in the second half of fiscal 2026, heightens the challenge of managing supply, demand and inventory and could adversely affect revenue and inventory management.
Demand for AI products depends on how customers use generative AI, whose near-term and long-term trajectory is unknown. Some customers may lack access to data center capacity or energy for buildouts.

Warrants for up to 160 million shares each at $0.01 per share, issued to OpenAI and Meta, vest on GPU purchase milestones and stock-price conditions. They are classified as liabilities until conditions for equity classification are met, so dilution and fair-value swings are possible. No warrant shares had vested as of June 27, 2026.

Earnings quality: Other income (expense), net rose to $763 million for six months, mainly from unrealized gains on newly public equity stakes. $1.1 billion of marketable equity securities are subject to time-based sale restrictions expiring through October 2028, so these gains are non-operating and may be volatile.

Export controls: prior-year results included inventory and related charges tied to U.S. government export controls on MI308 Data Center GPU products, showing geopolitical sensitivity of China-related sales.

bull_case: Data Center net revenue more than doubled to $6.7 billion (+107% YoY), driven by strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct MI350 Series GPUs, and the segment swung to $2.1 billion of operating income from a $155 million loss.

Total net revenue rose 50% to $11.5 billion, with operating income of $2.0 billion vs a $134 million loss and gross margin of 54% vs 40%. Operating leverage is visible as revenue growth outpaced opex growth.

Multi-year agreements with OpenAI and Meta, each intending to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs with the first gigawatt on MI450, give the second-half Helios and MI450 ramp a very large potential base that is not yet in reported revenue.

The balance sheet is strong: $13.1 billion of cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, total debt principal of $3.25 billion, an undrawn revolver and a higher $5.5 billion commercial paper ceiling.
Operating cash flow of $5.3 billion in six months more than doubled from $2.4 billion in continuing operations a year ago, funding capex of $1.2 billion without new borrowing.
Embedded revenue grew 19% to $977 million with operating income of $386 million vs $275 million, and Client revenue grew 23% on 34% unit growth, showing breadth outside Data Center.
Milestone-vesting warrants align OpenAI and Meta with AMD's volume and share price, and no tranches have vested, so dilution occurs only if AMD wins the GPU volume.
bear_case: The 14-point gross margin gain is largely a comparison effect: the filing credits the absence of the prior-year MI308 export-control charge first and favorable mix second, with no quantified split. Margin missed the roughly 56% consensus and the stock fell about 8% after the print.

The filing warns of an industry-wide memory shortage and rising memory prices that could raise production costs and pressure gross margin in coming quarters, when the comparison tailwind no longer applies.

Earnings quality is flattered by non-operating items: Other income (expense), net rose $626 million to $763 million for six months on unrealized gains from newly listed equity stakes, and these shares carry sale restrictions through October 2028.

Fixed obligations are large: $30.3 billion of unconditional commitments ($17.4 billion in the rest of 2026), $4.1 billion of data center lease guarantees, $4.5 billion of leases not yet commenced and $9.5 billion of future data center lease payments. These are exposed if the AI buildout slows.

Customers may lack capital for AI infrastructure and seek deferred-payment arrangements, and AMD's 6 GW programs reflect customer intent rather than committed purchase orders. A small number of customers account for a substantial part of revenue.
R&D grew 33% and marketing, general and administrative grew about 41% against 50% revenue growth, so operating leverage may be less clean than headline margins suggest.

Client revenue growth is volume-led with a 6% ASP decline, Gaming fell 31%, and Client and Gaming operating income fell to $582 million from $767 million despite higher revenue. Accounts receivable rose $966 million in six months, a working-capital build that flatters nothing about cash conversion.

what_to_watch.text:
**Gross Margin Durability:** The 10-Q reports a 54% gross margin vs 40% a year ago, but attributes the increase first to the absence of the prior-year MI308 export-control inventory charge and second to favorable mix. The result missed the roughly 56% consensus for non-GAAP margin and the stock fell about 8%, and the filing warns that memory shortages and rising memory prices could pressure margin. On the other hand, Data Center revenue more than doubled and mix is a genuine tailwind, so 54% may prove a credible floor rather than a one-off.

-> Monitor management's charge-adjusted gross margin bridge, the GAAP vs non-GAAP reconciliation (the roughly 56% non-GAAP guide), and commentary on memory cost inflation.

**Data Center Momentum and Operating Leverage:** Data Center revenue rose 107% to $6.7 billion on EPYC and MI350 demand, the segment earned $2.1 billion of operating income, and the roughly $13 billion Q3 revenue outlook implies a further sequential step-up. That said, part of the margin expansion is a base effect, R&D grew 33% and marketing, general and administrative about 41% against 50% revenue growth, and $30.3 billion of unconditional commitments plus customer-concentration risk could squeeze returns if the ramp slows. The filing shows these as disclosed risks rather than current weakness, so the demand case is intact but the margin case is less settled.

-> Monitor Data Center sequential growth vs the roughly $13 billion Q3 guide, segment operating margin, and whether R&D growth stays below revenue growth.

**MI450 / Helios Ramp:** Q2 Data Center growth came from EPYC and MI350, so the MI450 and Helios rack-scale generation, with OpenAI and Meta each intending to deploy up to 6 gigawatts and the first gigawatt on MI450, is upside not yet in reported revenue. Management has indicated production shipments begin at the end of Q3 with a very significant step-up in Q4. However, the 6 GW figures are customer intent rather than purchase orders, and the filing flags supply, demand and inventory management challenges with the Helios rollout in the second half.

-> Monitor MI450 revenue recognition timing, Helios shipment commentary, inventory build and any change to the Q4 step-up language.

**Earnings Quality and Cash Conversion:** Six-month net income of $3.68 billion more than doubled, but Other income (expense), net rose $626 million to $763 million on unrealized gains from newly listed equity stakes, including $549 million of gains from long-term investments in the cash flow statement. Operating cash flow of $5.3 billion (vs $2.4 billion in continuing operations) is the stronger signal. However, it was supported by working-capital swings, with accounts receivable up $966 million and inventories up $548 million, so conversion should be judged against operating income rather than net income.

-> Monitor operating income, operating cash flow less capex, receivable and inventory trends, and any further mark-to-market gains on restricted equity holdings.

**Commitments, Leases and Liquidity:** AMD holds $13.1 billion of cash and short-term investments, an undrawn revolver, $3.25 billion of debt principal ($875 million current) and a commercial paper ceiling raised to $5.5 billion, which comfortably covers near-term needs. However, it reports $30.3 billion of unconditional commitments ($17.4 billion in the rest of 2026), $4.1 billion of data center lease guarantees, $4.5 billion of leases not yet commenced and capex of $1.2 billion in six months vs $494 million a year ago. These fixed claims could become a burden if AI deployments slip.

-> Monitor the commitments schedule, commercial paper usage, capex pace, and any new guarantees or capacity purchase agreements.

**Customer Warrants and Financing Structures:** Warrants for up to 160 million shares each at $0.01 were issued to OpenAI and Meta, vesting with GPU purchase milestones and stock-price hurdles, and no tranches have vested. This aligns customers with AMD's volume, and dilution arises only if AMD wins the deployments. On the other hand, the warrants are classified as liabilities, so fair-value swings could hit earnings as the stock rises, the revenue-accounting treatment remains an open question, and the filing notes customers may seek deferred-payment arrangements.

-> Monitor warrant fair-value charges, any contra-revenue treatment disclosed, vesting progress, and commentary on customer financing arrangements.

**Client and Gaming Profitability:** Client revenue rose 23% to $3.1 billion on 34% unit growth, but average selling price fell 6%, and Gaming declined 31% to $779 million on lower semi-custom revenue. Client and Gaming operating income fell to $582 million from $767 million despite revenue up 6%. The recovering PC market supports volume, but pricing and gaming weakness are drags on segment returns.

-> Monitor Client ASP trends, semi-custom outlook, and Client and Gaming operating margin.
